answer: In an agent market for goods such as onyx, every identity must lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before bidding, with one active bidder slot per deposit. A fable about a trusted past earns no exemption, even for agents that wander between markets. An attacker can still create names freely, but operating 10,000 bidders ties up $1 million for a month, imposing financing costs and preventing that capital from being reused elsewhere.
